Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

via preposition

by way of a place or a route

also by way of, by (a road, a route)

classical

Vulg. Mt. 2.12: per aliam viam reversī sunt
Caes. BG 1.6.1: ūnum per Sēquanōs

per (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

via, by way of, through

The way taken, through a land or by a road: per Sēquanōs, through the land of the Sequani; per aliam viam, by another road.

Other words

  • viā Appiā, terrā marīque (ablative alone) — by (a road, by land, by sea)

    ablative of the way, without a preposition · classical · Hor. S. 1.9.1: ībam forte viā Sacrā

    The road, gate or element one travels by stands in the ablative: viā Appiā, by the Appian Way; portā exīre, go out by the gate; terrā marīque, by land and sea.

Examples

  • per aliam viam reversī sunt in regiōnem suam

    they went back to their own country by another roadVulg. Mt. 2.12

  • Erant omnīnō itinera duo, quibus itineribus domō exīre possent: ūnum per Sēquanōs, angustum et difficile

    there were only two routes by which they could leave home: one via the Sequani, narrow and difficultCaes. BG 1.6.1

  • ībam forte viā Sacrā, sīcut meus est mōs

    I happened to be going by the Sacred Way, as is my habitHor. S. 1.9.1

See also through, along.
